task_intent: Refine five Tessera games with expressive native boards and matching wall compositions.
mobbin_queries: Reaction time test game showing milliseconds and a large tap target
Arcade game with character, score and touch controls

mobbin.observed: A dark racing reaction screen groups four signal lights above a very large timing readout, a quiet ready label and a bright play button.
mobbin.applied: Give the signal and timing their own uninterrupted square stage. Distinguish open-circle ready, pause-bar wait and solid-target go states, with stable trial markers below. Keep results outside the active target.

mobbin.observed: A generous single central countdown number dominates the workout screen, while the current set and timing controls remain small and peripheral.
mobbin.applied: Use an expressive oversized reaction time with separate unit, calm surrounding instructions and a compact best/average ledger.

mobbin.observed: An illustrated sky is the continuous playfield; a score badge sits near the top, with a clear small foreground character and ample space around the action.
mobbin.applied: Draw one continuous midnight flight scene with a warm gold bird, moon, quiet stars and mint obstacles. Keep score separate from the bird and place steering controls outside the flight scene.

mobbin.observed: An illustrated mini-game announces its start with a large countdown and keeps the score and timer distinct from the game objects.
mobbin.applied: Give flight a deliberate safe ready phase and a separate stationary whistle-calibration phase. Begin movement only after input, and keep ready/result labels away from the bird and obstacle opening.

primary_web.title: Human Benchmark — Reaction Time Statistics
primary_web.applied: Explain that phone taps include display, input and network delay. Use the wall detector timestamp for direct knocks, even when its event arrives before the green frame is rendered.

primary_web.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Designing for games
primary_web.applied: Use familiar large native controls alongside direct game interactions, legible out-of-scene instructions, and explicit state/result feedback.

primary_web.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Game controls
primary_web.applied: Support direct drag steering, a flight-height slider, large Climb and Descend buttons, and VoiceOver adjustable actions with an announced next opening.

primary_web.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Accessibility
primary_web.applied: Provide non-colour signal shapes and written phase names, responsive Dynamic Type controls, 44-point minimum touch targets, spoken start/end feedback and accessible alternate steering.

primary_web.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Motion
primary_web.applied: Interpolate only between received authoritative poses for at most 120ms, then hold. Reduce Motion disables interpolation. A long wall physics stall pauses instead of advancing unseen action.

assets: Original native vector scenes and matching production Python RGB geometry. No third-party reference images are included in application assets.

validation.scope: Timing, finite payloads, calibration, touch steering, collision extents and sweep, pause/resume, scoring, complete receipts and RGB geometry. Root integration owns native builds, captures, deployment and physical hardware review.
